notes.text: WORKFLOW: split rhythm under constant light. Under constant light the circadian system can bifurcate: two oscillator components decouple, run at slightly different periods, and re-stabilise roughly 12 h apart. Here the two components are supplied separately (24.8 h and 23.4 h) and the actograph record is their SUM, so the split you see emerges from the two oscillators drifting apart rather than being drawn in. Read the component actogram alongside the recorded one to see where the second band comes from. The periodogram gives the numeric signature: two peaks rather than one, which is what should make you suspect splitting in a real record even before it is obvious by eye.
